recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Broader negation-model or absent-status questions should remain under their own Jira decisions rather than reopening this already-applied DSTU2 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-11077 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2. It asked how to assert that a subject does not have a condition and approved adding Condition usage guidance with two exceptions: a refuted Condition record when a prior belief was later refuted, and checklist questions represented with QuestionnaireResponse or Observation rather than Condition.
initial_application: Commit 87f224c94cabbf01ee3789f815f26c69d05608d4 explicitly applied #11077 by adding the Assertions of Condition Absence section to source/condition/condition-notes.xml. Commit 005f3df50afc07ae825c55698ac247ac81eb4882 later restored condition-notes.xml after it had been unintentionally deleted.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini, making source/condition/condition-notes.xml current build-scope source. Later related decisions refined but did not reverse the guidance: FHIR-11026 clarified the refuted-condition bullet with Condition.verificationStatus and Condition.evidence, FHIR-14871 rejected a distinct absent status, and FHIR-26904 clarified Condition versus Observation boundaries and is already audited on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Condition notes contain the Assertions of Condition Absence heading and both approved exceptions, with later wording that more precisely distinguishes refuted Condition records from general absence assertions while preserving the QuestionnaireResponse-or-Observation checklist guidance.
